newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev closes weaker near 2,500 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev closes weaker near 2,500 per dollar.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 2,450-2,550 per dollar, down from the morning's 2,350-2,450 and 1,930-2,000 at Friday's close as interbank trade was limited to low volumes due to general reluctance to sell, dealers said.
"Foreign currency demand from banks and clients was low but supply was even lower. Traders were not willing to sell because of the rapid lev depreciation," said a dealer.
The market was very nervous and dollar bids for volumes as low as $50,000-$100,000 immediately erased another 100-200 levs off the value of the local currency.
The lev firmed a little at exchange shops in the afternoon due to a slight fall in dollar demand, traders said.
"People continue withdrawing their savings from banks but now they seem to be more concerned with buying food rather than converting levs into dollars," said a trader at an exchange bureau in Sofia.

The dollar was bid at 1,600-1,800 levs around 1600 local time (1400 GMT) and was offered at 2,100-2,300 levs at exchange shops, down from midday's 2,500-2,700. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
